translation:
Catching wind-cold or failing to resolve the exterior, it turns into vexing fever disturbing the heart. There is also vexing fever of a different category — yang deficiency with yin excess, which one should know.
Yang excess causes chaotic vexatious heat of the heart; yin deficiency causes anger and vexed agitation of the kidney. Vexation (fan) is mild heat, agitation (zao) is severe heat; vexation and agitation, which comes first and which is dryness versus vexation, distinguish them.
translator_notes: 煩=fán (vexation, mild restlessness); 躁=zào (agitation, severe restlessness).
The last couplet distinguishes 煩熱 (mild) from 燥熱 (severe).
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Wind damage fears wind, cold damage fears cold; when the interstices (couli) are not dense the pathogen gains entry. Aversion to wind belongs wholly to yang and harmonious qi, not comparable to yin-yang giving aversion to cold.
There is also cold damage with aversion to wind of the back; the back is the meeting of yang, the abdomen is yin. Making the back fear cold, yang is insufficient; Qianghu Chonghe is the one that must be followed.
translator_notes: 腠理=couli (interstices between skin and muscles).
背為陽會=the back is the gathering of yang; 腹為陰=abdomen is yin.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Cold damage headache and dizziness are not like common location-invoked ones. When the pathogen is at Sun (Taiyang) the head must ache; for exertion of the bedchamber illness only supplementation is made lord.
If it is a convalescing case with body pain, inducing sweat that injures yang turns into wind. There is also inability of the four limbs to move freely; before and after the illness, supplementation and drainage are to be distinguished.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
